scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from July (590) to August (1180) and stayed elevated into September (1260).
Disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL read type (1,785) over ESTIMATED (1,240).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026.
Dispute ticket response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) throughout the surge.
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Since August 2026, billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled (590→1180→1260/month, E-07) primarily because the billing import/validation step of the meter-to-cash process is producing incorrect bills on accounts with ACTUAL meter reads (1,785 of 3,025 disputed bills) more often than on estimate-substituted bills (1,240) (E-01). This rules out slower ticket handling as the driver (response times stay within the 3.0-day SLA, E-02) and points away from read-collection failure as the dominant cause, leaving a defect in bill production from valid reads as the best-supported mechanism; a reported field-staffing shortfall (E-04/E-06) separately explains part of the smaller estimated-read-bill cohort.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem that an AI auto-answer agent would resolve, independent of whether bills themselves are wrong.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI meter reads from the vendor (MDMS) are failing to deliver or validate correctly, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter reads are failing to arrive or validate (upload/semantic issues), causing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A shortage of field reading staff/contract headcount since August reduced route completion, indirectly causing missed reads and bill errors.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: Billing import validation specifically rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and disputes even when the AMI read itself was received and exported correctly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db shows disputed bills split by read type: 1,785 with read_type ACTUAL and 1,240 with read_type ESTIMATED, so disputes occur more often on bills that had an actual meter read than on ones using an estimated substitute reading.
CRM data on 2,440 dispute tickets shows median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA, so ticket-handling speed is not currently a problem for the dispute surge.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, so no tariff/rate change is recorded as having occurred; this rules out a tariff change as a cause of wrong bills. Note this log is distinct from the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES, billing-config) that H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE depends on, which remains unqueried.

Route-log data shows manual meter-reading routes achieved only 88% completion against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts during Aug-Sep 2026, confirming a measurable field read-collection shortfall coinciding with the dispute surge period.

Route-log still shows manual-read routes at 88% completion against a 95% target across 9,200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (observation unchanged), but it no longer supports the premise that this field read-collection shortfall explains part of the disputed ESTIMATED-cohort bills, since E-12 shows 95.5% of that cohort had AMI reads received and exported but rejected by billing import, not missing manual reads.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's unverified claim that no tariff change occurred this year echoes the already-established tool finding (E-03) that billing-db's tariff_change_log has zero records; it adds no new decision-relevant information beyond corroborating that record.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a shortage of three readers since July has caused routes to run late, resulting in estimated bills for affected customers; this is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a causal explanation for the route completion shortfall already measured in E-04, not new tool evidence. SH-FIELD has a stated incentive toward contract headcount increase and a noted bias to attribute problems to staffing, so this claim should be weighed cautiously pending independent verification.

SH-FIELD's statement that a 3-reader shortage since July causes late routes and estimated bills still stands as a recorded, unverified stakeholder claim (observation unchanged), but it no longer credibly explains the ESTIMATED-cohort dispute surge, since E-12 shows the dominant mechanism (95.5% of that cohort) is billing-import rejection of received AMI reads, not missing field reads from understaffing.

CRM monthly dispute counts (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep 2026) show volume was flat around 600/month then roughly doubled starting in August and stayed elevated into September, confirming the surge's timing and magnitude but saying nothing about its cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (§4.2) confirms the utility may request route priority changes, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD); this is the documentary basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update, not new causal information about the billing dispute surge.

U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.question: Did the billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES, billing-config) show a change around August 2026 that explains the pattern of errors on ACTUAL-read bills?
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix is a billing-config rule correction requiring SH-BILL escalation versus a different mechanism, and whether any bill-write action could ever be scoped.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query the billing-config tool for the rule-change log around August 2026 and cross-reference with disputed-bill timestamps.
U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the actual-read billing-error cause as unconfirmed; do not propose or authorize any automated bill write until the rule-change log is reviewed.

U-METRIC-VALIDITY-TICKET-VOLUM.question: Would reducing dispute-ticket creation (e.g., via an auto-answer agent) lower dispute_volume_monthly without actually correcting bills, invalidating it as a proxy for G-1 (correct bills)?
U-METRIC-VALIDITY-TICKET-VOLUM.decision_impact: If so, dispute_volume_monthly alone cannot certify success and must be paired with an independent billing-accuracy or re-dispute-rate check.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY-TICKET-VOLUM.resolution_path: Track re-dispute/reopened-ticket rate and disputed_bill_actual_share alongside raw volume before declaring G-1 met.
U-METRIC-VALIDITY-TICKET-VOLUM.safe_placeholder: Report dispute volume together with disputed_bill_actual_share and route completion; do not treat volume decline alone as proof of fixed bills.

U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-SCOPE.question: How much of the estimated-read-bill dispute cohort (1,240) would be resolved by closing the reported 3-reader shortfall, versus other causes, given SH-FIELD's incentive toward headcount increase?
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-SCOPE.decision_impact: Affects whether field dispatch/staffing remediation is prioritized and how much it is expected to reduce dispute volume.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-SCOPE.resolution_path: Correlate route-log completion gaps per route with the subset of estimated-read disputed-bill accounts to quantify the staffing-attributable share.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Treat field staffing shortage as a confirmed but partial contributor affecting only the estimated-read minority of disputes until quantified.
U-STAFFING-SHORTAGE-SCOPE.resolution: E-12 shows only 56 of the 1,240 ESTIMATED-cohort disputed bills (4.5%) had no AMI read received at all (potentially staffing/read-collection related); the remaining 1,184 (95.5%) had reads received and exported but rejected by billing import for high consumption, a cause unrelated to the staffing shortfall.

A-DEFECT-LOCATED-IN-BILLING-IM.statement: Elimination of AMI/field read failures and ticket-handling delay (E-01, E-02) implies the billing-error source lies in billing import/validation rather than upstream read collection; this location is inferred, not directly observed.

A-STAFFING-CLAIM-RELIABILITY.statement: SH-FIELD's claim of a 3-reader shortage since July (E-06) is assumed materially accurate despite SH-FIELD's stated incentive toward contract headcount increase.
